exam.title: Design and Technology Paper 1 (17/1) - October/November 2025
exam.subject: Design and Technology
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: Which type of line is used for outlines?
questions.explanation: Visible outlines and edges are drawn with a thick continuous line. Short dashes show hidden detail, long chain lines show centre lines, and a zig-zag line marks a break.

questions.question: Which plastic is most resistant to wearing?
questions.explanation: Nylon is tough, has a low-friction surface and resists abrasion, which is why it is used for gears, bearings and bushes that rub against other parts.

questions.question: Which of the following specifications addresses the function of a CD rack?
questions.explanation: The function of a product is the job it does. A CD rack's job is to hold and store CDs; playing, cleaning and recording are done by other products.

questions.question: Which method of timber conversion is shown by the illustration below?
questions.explanation: The log is first cut into four quarters, and boards are then cut from each quarter so the cuts run roughly along the radius. This is quarter sawing, which gives stable, attractive boards but wastes more timber.

questions.question: Which manufactured board is shown below?
questions.explanation: The edge shows a core of solid wooden strips glued side by side and covered on both faces with a veneer. That construction is block board.

questions.question: Which is the appropriate tool for marking lines parallel to the edge of a metal?
questions.explanation: Odd leg (jenny) callipers have one bent leg that runs along the edge of the metal while the pointed leg scribes a parallel line. A marking gauge does the same job on wood.

questions.question: Which tool is most suitable to check for the flatness of a surface?
questions.explanation: The straight blade of a try square is laid across the surface in several directions; light showing under the blade reveals where the surface is not flat. It is the tool used for testing both flatness and squareness.

questions.question: Which of the following grades of abrasives is arranged in the correct order?
options: Medium, coarse, fine, super coarse, extra fine
Super coarse, coarse, medium, fine, extra fine
Super coarse, extra fine, coarse, fine, medium
Fine, medium, extra fine, coarse, super coarse
questions.explanation: Abrasive grades run in sequence from the roughest to the smoothest: super coarse, coarse, medium, fine, extra fine. Only option B follows that order.

questions.question: Before applying varnish onto wood, the surface should be
questions.explanation: The surface is abraded (sanded smooth with glass paper, working through the grades) so the varnish goes on evenly and the final finish is smooth.

questions.question: Which class of file is shown in the diagram below?
questions.explanation: The file is long, flat and parallel, with a tang fitted into a handle. That is a hand file. Needle files are very small, a rasp has individual raised teeth, and a Surform has a perforated blade in a frame.

questions.question: Which finish is used to improve the colour of wood?
questions.explanation: A wood stain soaks into the timber and changes or enriches its colour while still showing the grain. Varnish, oil and sealer mainly protect the surface.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations shows commercially available sections of metals?
questions.explanation: Metals are sold as bar, tube, rod and sheet (also strip and angle). Film, board, ply, fibre and reed are not forms in which metal is supplied.

questions.question: Which force describes compression?
questions.explanation: Compression is a squashing or pushing force that tends to shorten a part. Pulling is tension, twisting is torsion and curving is bending.

questions.question: Which of the following diagrams shows the correct division of line GH in the ratio 2:4?
questions.explanation: To divide a line in a ratio, draw a construction line from G, step off equal divisions along it with dividers, join the last division to H and draw lines parallel to that join back onto GH. Diagram B shows this: the divisions are marked on the construction line and projected back with parallel lines. In A the marks are on GH itself, C marks both lines, and D has no stepped-off divisions.

questions.question: What is the name of the part labelled S on the pair of shears shown below?
questions.explanation: S points to the bolt where the two halves of the shears are joined and turn. That is the pivot point.

questions.question: Which of the following is a basic requirement when marking out on a flat wood surface?
options: One edge should always be flat.
The surface and the edge should always be flat.
The surface should be flat, and one edge should be square to the surface.
questions.explanation: Marking out starts from a face side (a flat surface) and a face edge planed square to it. All measurements and lines are taken from these two datum surfaces.

questions.question: What is the use of a tang on a file?
options: To hold when using the file
To connect the blade to the handle
To prevent the handle from splitting
To prevent ferrule from becoming loose
questions.explanation: The tang is the pointed end of the file that is driven into the handle, connecting the blade to it. A file must never be used without a handle on the tang.

questions.question: Which of the following shows construction of 30° angle?
questions.explanation: A 30° angle is made by first constructing 60° (an arc from the vertex, then the same radius stepped off along it) and then bisecting that 60°. Diagram B shows the 60° line drawn faintly and the bisector drawn as the final 30° line.

questions.question: Why should the work piece be firmly clamped when drilling?
options: To prevent the table from moving
To prevent the drill bit from moving
To prevent the work piece from moving
To prevent someone from holding the work piece
questions.explanation: The turning drill can snatch the work and spin it round, which is dangerous and spoils the hole. Clamping holds the work piece still.

questions.question: Which of the following is an electronic symbol for a Light Emitting Diode?
questions.explanation: An LED is drawn as a diode (a triangle against a bar) with two arrows pointing away to show light being given out. B is a resistor, C is a lamp and D is a cell.

questions.question: Which mechanism can be used for an automatic sliding gate?
questions.explanation: A motor turns a pinion that meshes with a toothed rack fixed along the gate, converting rotary motion into the straight-line motion that slides the gate open and shut.

questions.question: Which method is suitable for joining two pieces of mild steel when making a burglar door?
questions.explanation: Welding melts and fuses the steel parts together, giving the strong, permanent joint a burglar door needs. Soldering and brazing are much weaker.

questions.question: Which of the following is suitable for joining rubber to metal?
questions.explanation: Contact adhesive is spread on both surfaces, left to become touch-dry and then pressed together. It bonds flexible materials such as rubber and leather to metal. PVA is for wood.

questions.question: Which type of chisel is suitable for finishing off dovetail joints?
questions.explanation: A paring chisel is long and thin and is pushed by hand (never struck) to take fine shavings, so it is used to clean up and finish joints such as dovetails.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about energy conservation in the home?
options: Always keep the air conditioner on to control the room temperature.
Always keep the geyser on to have hot water readily available.
Use an electric stove instead of kettle to boil water.
Turn off electric lights when not in use.
questions.explanation: Switching off lights that are not needed saves electricity. The other options all waste energy.

questions.question:
The steps for constructing a square EFGH are listed below, not in order:

i. Construct perpendiculars at points E and F.
ii. Draw a line EF to a given measurement.
iii. Using the same distance EF as radius step off points G and H.
iv. Join points G and H to complete the square.

Which of the following shows the correct order of steps?
questions.explanation: First draw the base EF (ii), then raise perpendiculars at E and F (i), mark G and H on them using EF as the radius (iii), and finally join G and H (iv).

questions.question: Which of the following will promote sales of a product?
questions.explanation: Advertising makes more people aware of the product and want it, which promotes sales. Raising prices usually reduces sales.

questions.question: What type of pictorial drawing is represented by the figure below?
questions.explanation: The receding edges of the table run towards two vanishing points marked on the horizon line, one at each side. That is two-point perspective.

questions.question: What is the main role of research in the design process?
options: To understand the identified problem in detail and come up with a solution
To acquire more knowledge and understanding of research
To guide designers to produce a product
To recognise people as future designers
questions.explanation: Research gathers information about the problem, the users and existing products so the designer understands the problem fully and can develop a suitable solution.

questions.question: Which materials are suitable for making a model of the bridge truss shown below?
questions.explanation: A truss is a frame of straight, rigid members joined together. Straws or sticks make the members and sellotape joins them. Thread, wool and fur cannot form rigid members.

questions.question: What is the use of electricity?
questions.explanation: Electricity is a form of energy used to provide power for lighting, heating and running machines. Solar, coal and gas are sources of energy, not uses of electricity.

questions.question: What factor will influence the drilling speed and feed on metal?
options: The use of cutting fluid will make the cutting process harder.
The harder the work the slower the cutting speed.
The harder the drill the faster the cutting speed.
The smaller drill has a greater surface speed.
questions.explanation: Harder materials must be drilled at a slower speed, otherwise the drill overheats and blunts. Cutting fluid makes cutting easier, not harder.

questions.question: The diagram shows a gear train. Which of the gears will turn clockwise if gear Z turns in a clockwise direction?
questions.explanation: Meshing gears turn in opposite directions. Z (clockwise) drives T anticlockwise. T drives both Q and S, so they turn clockwise. S drives R anticlockwise. The clockwise gears are therefore S and Q.

questions.question: A current of 1.2 amps goes through a light bulb which has a resistance of 9 ohms. What is the voltage applied?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: V = I × R = 1.2 A × 9 Ω = 10.8 V.

questions.question: Which material is correctly matched with its source?
questions.explanation: Soapstone is a soft rock that is quarried. Clay comes from soil, leather from animal skin and reed from plants.

questions.question: Which of the following tools is most suitable to drive the head of a hexagonal bolt?
questions.explanation: A ring spanner fits right round the six flats of the hexagonal head, so it grips firmly without slipping or rounding the corners.

questions.question: Which of the following is a holding device?
questions.explanation: A vice clamps and holds work steady. A drill, plane and saw are cutting tools.

questions.question: The figure shows part of a working model of a crane. Which mechanism has been used in the figure?
questions.explanation: The spiral, screw-like worm on the upright shaft meshes with the large toothed wheel. This worm and worm wheel gives a large speed reduction and stops the load running back, which suits a crane.

questions.question: Which drawing technique is illustrated below?
questions.explanation: The sphere is shaded with a smooth change from light to dark, with a highlight where the light falls. That is tone shading. No lines or hatching are used.

questions.question: The diagram shows an isometric projection of a block. Which of the following diagrams represents an orthographic projection of the block?
questions.explanation: Each view must show every visible edge of the block in its correct position and line up with the other views. Compare the front view, end view and plan of each option against the isometric drawing.
